prs.title: [ci] Reject focused Playwright tests in Flight fixture
prs.author: chengchuu

prs.title: [Flight] Fix reviving errors without stack frames in debug info
prs.author: lazerg
prs.body:
## Summary

`serializeDebugErrorValue` outlines the error info with `objectLimit: stack.length * 2 + 1`, but the error info object itself uses one from that budget. With zero frames the limit is 1, so the empty `stack` array gets deferred and goes out as `"$Y"`. The client then gets a string placeholder where it expects an array, `buildFakeCallStack` throws on it, and the error fails to revive. For an `AggregateError` that failure leaves `errors` as `null`, so `AggregateError(null, ...)` throws during parsing and the root never resolves.

Errors from Node internals (like the `ECONNREFUSED` from happy eyeballs in the issue) have no frames, so they hit this when they show up as a rejected I/O value or in a replayed log. Bumping the limit by one leaves room for the stack array itself.

Fixes #37728

## How did you test this change?

- Added a test that logs an `AggregateError` wrapping a frameless error and checks that it gets replayed. It fails on main (the log is never replayed) and passes with the fix.
- Ran the repro from the issue against 19.3.0 with the same one-line change applied to the published server bundle: the root now resolves to `"handled: all failed"` instead of throwing `object null is not iterable`.
- `yarn test packages/react-client packages/react-server packages/react-server-dom-webpack`. The only failure, `ReactFlightDOMEdge › should break up large sync components...`, also fails on main locally.

prs.title: [flags] Cleanup enableFragmentRefsInstanceHandles and enableFragmentRefsTextNodes feature flags
prs.author: javache
prs.body:
Both flags are fully rolled out. This removes the flag definitions from all forks, drops the conditionals (keeping the enabled behavior), and removes the @gate pragmas from ReactDOMFragmentRefs tests.

Test plan: ReactDOMFragmentRefs tests pass on source, www, and www variant-false channels; ESLint, Prettier, and Flow (dom-node, fabric) pass.
